## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fóshuō Sūnduōyézhì jīng* (T582) is a one-fascicle short sūtra translated by Zhī Qiān 支謙 ([支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99)). *Sūnduōyézhì* 孫多耶致 transcribes the Indic name Sundarika(bhāradvāja) — the brahmin known from the Pāli *Sundarikabhāradvāja-sutta* (SN 7.9 / Sn 3.4), who debates with the Buddha over the value of ritual bathing in sacred rivers.

**Abstract**

A short *Saṃyukta-āgama* / *Sutta-nipāta*-type narrative on the futility of bathing in sacred rivers as a means of purification. Datable to Zhī Qiān's Wú-period activity (222–252 CE). Counterparts: Pāli *Sundarikabhāradvāja-sutta* (Sn 3.4) and *Saṃyukta-āgama* parallels.
